The inscriptions of early Satavahana kings were found in
x:
The earliest inscriptions of the Satavahanas have been discovered mainly in Maharashtra, indicating that the dynasty initially established its political base in the western Deccan before expanding eastward into Andhra. Important early Satavahana inscriptions include those found at Naneghat and Nasik, both located in present-day Maharashtra. The Naneghat Inscription, issued by Queen Naganika, wife of Satakarni I, provides valuable information about the genealogy of the early Satavahana rulers and the Vedic sacrifices performed by the king. Similarly, the Nasik Cave Inscriptions, particularly that of Gautami Balasri, mother of Gautamiputra Satakarni, are among the most important sources for Satavahana political history. Although the Satavahanas later ruled large parts of Andhra Pradesh and contributed significantly to the development of Amaravati and Dharanikota, their earliest inscriptional evidence comes from Maharashtra.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (1).
